clue.text: Resort to richer language to impress

indicators.note: read as re-sort, sorting the following letters over again into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone falls back on fancier words to show off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like 'fall back on', but read it as re-sort: TO RICHER rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is persuasive or showy speech, the art of using words for effect.

clue.text: Many a dog deprived of love gets angry

indicators.note: deprived of says a letter is taken away from the dog word

parts.note: a hound is a dog
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
someone angry is red in the face

explanation.surface: A dog robbed of affection turns nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived of' removes O from HOUND, leaving HUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred is a large number, so it can stand for many things.

clue.text: Run into the quiet, dilapidated entrance

indicators.note: into says the run letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
sh is the call for quiet
something dilapidated is old and worn

explanation.surface: Someone dashes into a hushed, crumbling doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is the sill of a doorway, the point of entry to a house.

clue.text: Traveller to dine — and do it again

parts.note: a commercial traveller is a sales rep
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A salesman eats dinner and then wants another helping.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat an action is to perform it once more.

clue.text: Which reporter's name upset an architect?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the S of the possessive is used as a letter here

explanation.surface: A question about which journalist's article annoyed a building designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles WHICH and REPORTERS into CHRISTOPHERWRE; here the possessive S counts as a letter. N for name ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral in London, the most famous English architect.

clue.text: Child holding mother back — they're ramblers

indicators.note: back says the whole assembled piece is read in the opposite direction
holding says the child word keeps the mother word inside it

parts.note: a son is a child
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A youngster carries a parent on their back, and the group is out walking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the whole of SDAMON, not just the mother; the surface makes it sound like a piggyback.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads wander from place to place, roaming like hikers without a fixed home.

clue.text: Direct noisy workman to the exit

indicators.note: noisy says the workman word is heard rather than seen, giving its sound

parts.note: a navvy is a British labourer digging roads or canals
a gate is a way out

explanation.surface: Telling a loud labourer to leave by the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: A NAVVY is a British manual labourer; 'noisy' gives its sound, spelt NAVI.
explanation.definitionFit: To navigate a vessel is to steer or guide its course.

clue.text: When one is accommodated in a hotel, extravagance initially is foolish

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

indicators.note: accommodated in says the one letter is lodged inside the hotel word

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A guest staying at a hotel splashes out and looks silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means stupid, as daft as an ass.

clue.text: Vest worn by one in a suit

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: Someone wears a vest under a business suit.
explanation.walkthrough: The suit is a suit of cards: a singleton is a lone card of its suit in a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a singleton is the only card held in a particular suit.

clue.text: Mate upset — king escapes snare

indicators.note: upset says the remaining letters are knocked into a new order
escapes says the king letter gets out of the mate word

parts.note: a mate is a partner
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A distressed partner notes the king slipping out of a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escapes' takes R from PARTNER, leaving PARTNE, which 'upset' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to catch them, as in a trap.

clue.text: Mugging up about a ghost

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a vision is an apparition or ghost

explanation.surface: Someone is robbed while worrying about a spook.
explanation.definitionFit: Revision is study for an exam, the same as cramming.

clue.text: Well covered by hair in fringe, in a word

indicators.note: covered by says the well word sits inside the hair word

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a mineral spring or well

explanation.surface: A water source hidden beneath a fringe of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a word' tells you to join 'in fringe' into one word, infringe.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to infringe, to break a rule or overstep a boundary.

clue.text: Some oxygen I allow to get warm

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Letting in a little oxygen to heat something up.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'to get warm' is a verb phrase and cannot replace an adjective; 'to get' is a link and 'warm' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Genial means friendly and cordial, a warm manner.

clue.text: I would love to be in it, that was natural

parts.note: I'd is short for I would

indicators.note: to be in says the love letter goes inside the it word

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone longs to be included, as it seemed instinctive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'natural' is an old word for a person born simple-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural, in old usage, was a simpleton born lacking in wits.

clue.text: He's succeeded in transmuting their iron

indicators.note: transmuting means changing form, as an alchemist changes metal, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: An alchemist triumphs in turning their iron into something else.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is one who follows a previous owner into a title or property.

clue.text: Temperate zone

explanation.surface: A geography lesson on climate bands.
explanation.definitionFit: Continent means self-restrained or moderate; it is also a large landmass or region of the world.

clue.text: A bet is on the cards here

definitions.text: A bet is on the cards here

parts.words: A bet is on the cards here
parts.note: read as a card game where stakes go on cards laid out, or as a Suffolk racing town where bets are placed

explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is both a card game with stakes laid on cards and the English town that is the home of horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a gambling card game and a racecourse town, both places for betting.

clue.text: Find record's finished

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
something finished is over

explanation.surface: A record has come to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something is to come upon it for the first time.

clue.text: Entering hilly area, leading amateur driver loses part of car

indicators.note: entering says the following letters go inside the hilly area word

parts.note: a height is high ground

indicators.note: leading picks the first letter of each of the following words

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lost in league tables

explanation.surface: An amateur racer, ahead into hill country, sheds a bit of the car.
explanation.walkthrough: AD from 'leading' plus L (lost, from 'loses') enters HEIGHT: HE-ADL-IGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Headlights are the lamps on the front of a vehicle.

clue.text: Conducted an orchestra first, one not very successful

indicators.note: first says the earlier pieces come before the conducted word

parts.note: taken as written
LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra
to run a business is to conduct it, so ran

explanation.surface: Someone led an orchestra early in a career that never took off.
explanation.walkthrough: LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a horse or competitor that finishes out of the places, a loser.

clue.text: Mark two

explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain wrote Tom Sawyer; twain is an old word for a pair.

clue.text: Archipelago where I arrive in ship

definitions.note: a singular group noun defining a plural

indicators.note: in says the arrive word is placed inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS is short for steamship
to land is to arrive

explanation.surface: Someone describes reaching a chain of islands aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An archipelago is a group of islets scattered across a sea.

clue.text: Schoolchildren put up a boo-boo

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up says the word is written from the bottom upward

parts.note: schoolchildren are pupils

explanation.surface: Pupils make a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A boo-boo is a silly mistake, a blunder.

clue.text: Citrus flourishing in the country

indicators.note: flourishing as in waving about with a flourish, so the letters are thrown around

explanation.surface: Lemon trees thriving out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic describes things of rural life, belonging to the farmland.

clue.text: Engineers likely to be dependable

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
liable means likely, as in liable to rain

explanation.surface: Engineers are probably trustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliable means trustworthy, able to be counted on.

clue.text: Start running business

explanation.definitionFit: To turn over an engine is to get it going; a firm's turnover is its total volume of trade.

clue.text: Thrusting head of the river?

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
a king is a head of state

explanation.surface: Asking who leads the river, perhaps a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the Head of the River boat race; the head is a KING, of the PO.
explanation.definitionFit: Poking means jabbing or prodding forward.

clue.text: Spite voiced in private

indicators.note: voiced says the spite word is spoken aloud and heard

parts.note: rancour is spite or bitterness

explanation.surface: Ill will is expressed behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like 'secretly'; it is the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranker is a soldier in the ranks, an enlisted man rather than an officer.

clue.text: Special treatment involving pimentos

indicators.note: involving in its sense of entangling or twisting up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A menu offers a dish with peppers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism shown to relatives, especially in jobs.
